On the handtowelholder 1, you see a handtowel 1.</span></div></div><div class="scard"><div class="st">step 1</div><div class="io"><b>모델이 받은 것</b><span>위 관찰 + 스킬 + 최근 이력 1개 + 가능한 행동 17개.</span> <b>모델의 행동</b><span><code>take handtowel 1 from handtowelholder 1</code></span><b>환경의 답</b><span>You pick up the handtowel 1 from the handtowelholder 1.</span></div></div><div class="scard"><div class="st">step 2</div><div class="io"><b>모델이 받은 것</b><span>위 관찰 + 스킬 + 최근 이력 2개 + 가능한 행동 18개.</span> <b>모델의 행동</b><span><code>go to sinkbasin 1</code></span><b>환경의 답</b><span>다음 관찰이 이어집니다. 이 에피소드는 50스텝까지 갔고 실패했습니다.</span></div></div></div> <dl class="terms"> <dt>에피소드</dt><dd>게임 한 판입니다. 과제에 성공하거나 행동을 50번 하면 끝납니다.</dd> <dt>스텝</dt><dd>에피소드 안의 행동 한 번입니다. 스텝마다 모델에 요청을 한 번 보냅니다. 스텝 번호는 0부터 셉니다.</dd> <dt>카테고리</dt><dd>과제의 종류입니다. SkillRL은 과제 문장의 낱말을 보고 6종 중 하나를 고릅니다. 예를 들어 "clean"이 있으면 clean 카테고리입니다. 에피소드 안에서는 바뀌지 않습니다.</dd> <dt>스킬</dt><dd>프롬프트에 넣는 행동 요령 글입니다. 예: "Sink First for Cleaning: 물건을 들면 바로 싱크대로 가서 씻는다."</dd> <dt>스킬 뱅크</dt><dd>스킬을 모아 둔 JSON 파일입니다. SkillRL의 ALFWorld 뱅크에는 스킬 55개가 있습니다.</dd> <dt>프롬프트 구간</dt><dd>프롬프트 안에서 하는 일이 다른 부분입니다. 아래 그림에서 색이 다른 부분이 각 구간입니다.</dd> <dt>run</dt><dd>게임 64개를 동시에 끝까지 돌린 실험 한 번입니다.</dd> <dt>seed</dt><dd>모델이 응답을 고를 때 쓰는 난수의 시작값입니다. 모델은 다음 낱말을 확률에 따라 뽑습니다 (temperature 0.4). 그래서 seed가 다르면 같은 게임에서도 다른 응답과 행동이 나옵니다. 게임 64개는 seed와 관계없이 같습니다. 같은 조건을 seed 0·1·2로 세 번 돌리고 평균과 표준편차를 봅니다.</dd> </dl> <p>아래는 위 에피소드의 step 2 요청 전문입니다. 색은 구간의 종류를 나타냅니다. 숫자는 토큰 수입니다.</p> <div class="legend"><span><i class="sw-fixed"></i>고정 텍스트</span><span><i class="sw-task"></i>task 문장</span><span><i class="sw-skill"></i>스킬</span><span><i class="sw-hist"></i>이력</span><span><i class="sw-cur"></i>현재 관찰·행동 목록</span></div> <ol class='chips' aria-label='구간 순서와 토큰 수'><li class='chip'><i class='sw-fixed'></i>Qwen 기본 system 문장 <span class='n'>16</span></li><li class='chip'><i class='sw-fixed'></i>Role sentence <span class='n'>16</span></li><li class='chip'><i class='sw-task'></i>task 문장 <span class='n'>11</span></li><li class='chip'><i class='sw-skill'></i>General Principles <span class='n'>218</span></li><li class='chip'><i class='sw-skill'></i>카테고리 스킬 (Clean Skills) <span class='n'>375</span></li><li class='chip'><i class='sw-skill'></i>Mistakes to Avoid <span class='n'>278</span></li><li class='chip'><i class='sw-fixed'></i>Progress header (step count) <span class='n'>34</span></li><li class='chip'><i class='sw-hist'></i>이력 첫 항목 <span class='n'>148</span></li><li class='chip'><i class='sw-hist'></i>이력 둘째 항목 <span class='n'>54</span></li><li class='chip'><i class='sw-cur'></i>현재 관찰 <span class='n'>17</span></li><li class='chip'><i class='sw-cur'></i>가능한 행동 목록 <span class='n'>144</span></li><li class='chip'><i class='sw-fixed'></i>지시문 <span class='n'>67</span></li></ol> <pre class='prompt' tabindex='0'><span class='mk' title='chat template 토큰 · 3토큰'><|im_start|>system

</span><span class='hl-skill' title='General Principles · 218토큰'>### General Principles
- **Systematic Exploration**: Search every plausible surface or container exactly once before revisiting; prioritize unopened or unseen locations to cover the whole room methodically.
- **Immediate Acquisition**: As soon as a required object becomes visible and reachable, take it before moving elsewhere to avoid losing track or re-searching.
- **Destination First Policy**: After picking up a goal object, navigate directly to the known target receptacle and place it before resuming further search.
- **Track Counts & Progress**: Maintain an internal counter of how many goal objects are still needed; stop searching or terminate episode only when the counter reaches zero.
- **Use State-Changing Tools Early**: For tasks requiring heated/cooled/clean objects, acquire the object, then immediately use the nearest suitable appliance to change its state before any placement.
- **Establish Spatial Relations**: When a goal specifies a relation (under/inside/on), first locate the reference object, adjust its state if needed (e.g., turn lamp on), then search the specified spatial region for the target object or place it there.</span>

<span class='hl-skill' title='카테고리 스킬 (Clean Skills) · 375토큰'>### Clean Skills
- **Phase-Ordered Plan**: Always execute clean tasks in the fixed sequence: 1) locate & acquire target object, 2) bring it to an available water source/sink to clean, 3) navigate to final location, 4) place object.
  _Apply when: As soon as the goal specifies the object must be clean before placement._
- **Pick Before You Wander**: If the target object is visible or discovered, take it immediately; never leave it behind to explore other places, as possession enables direct cleaning and prevents redundant searches.
  _Apply when: After visually confirming the presence of the target object on any surface or inside an opened container._
- **Sink First for Cleaning**: Upon holding the target object, go straight to the nearest sink, basin, or faucet and issue the clean/use command before any placement attempts.
  _Apply when: Once the target object is in hand and its required state is ‘clean’._
- **Systematic Container Sweep**: When the object isn’t found on open surfaces, iterate through all unopened or unexamined containers in the room before revisiting already-checked spots to avoid search loops.
  _Apply when: After initial obvious surfaces are empty and the target object remains unfound._
- **State Verification Before Drop**: Always inspect or infer the object’s state after cleaning; if still not confirmed clean, re-clean before final placement to satisfy goal conditions.
  _Apply when: Immediately after a cleaning action and before placing the object at its target location._
- **Use Location Priors**: Begin search at the most probable category-specific surfaces (e.g., kitchenware on countertop/stove, food on dining table) to minimize exploration steps and avoid aimless roaming.
  _Apply when: At the very start of the task to choose the first search destination for the target object._</span>

<span class='hl-skill' title='Mistakes to Avoid · 278토큰'>### Mistakes to Avoid
- **Don't**: Agent repeatedly revisits the same already-searched locations or containers instead of exploring new ones.
  **Instead**: Maintain an exploration map that records which rooms/containers have been fully inspected and prioritize unvisited or unopened candidates until all reasonable options are exhausted.
- **Don't**: Agent decides a closed container is empty without opening it, causing missed discoveries of target objects.
  **Instead**: Always open and inspect every plausible closed container at least once before ruling it out, using a checklist of unopened containers in the current room.
- **Don't**: Agent ignores or walks away from target objects that are already visible and reachable.
  **Instead**: Embed a perception buffer that immediately queues pick-up actions for visible goal objects and interrupts any ongoing exploratory loop.
- **Don't**: Agent keeps searching after acquiring enough items because it loses track of how many targets have been collected.
  **Instead**: Maintain explicit numerical goals and increment/decrement them on every successful pickup or placement, triggering transition to the next sub-goal when counts are satisfied.
- **Don't**: Agent fails to deliver a held target object to the known destination, instead continuing to wander.
  **Instead**: Adopt a hierarchical policy that, upon holding a goal object, immediately switches to a high-priority ‘deliver-to-goal’ subtask before resuming further search.</span><span class='hl-fixed' title='Progress header (step count) · 34토큰'>

RL 모델이 SkillRL 논문의 최종 모델입니다.</p> <h2 id="t2" data-toc-text="1-2 세 논문: 무엇을 풀었고 어떻게 풀었나">1-2 세 논문: 무엇을 풀었고 어떻게 풀었나</h2> <p>세 시스템은 모두 경험에서 스킬을 만들고, 그 스킬을 프롬프트에 넣습니다. 가장 큰 차이는 무엇을 바꾸는가입니다. 아래 그림에서 주황 상자가 각 시스템이 바꾸는 쪽입니다.</p> <div class="sys" role="table" aria-label="세 시스템이 바꾸는 것"> <span class="h" role="columnheader"></span><span class="h" role="columnheader">경험을 정리하는 곳</span><span class="h" role="columnheader">스킬</span><span class="h" role="columnheader">실행 모델</span> <span class="n">SkillRL</span><span class="c na">없음 (궤적에서 바로 스킬)</span><span class="c">스킬 뱅크 55개. 평가 중에는 고정</span><span class="c chg">모델 가중치를 학습 (SFT → RL)</span> <span class="n">EvoSkill</span><span class="c na">없음 (실패한 답을 바로 분석)</span><span class="c chg">스킬 폴더를 만들고 고침</span><span class="c">고정 (Claude Code + Opus 4.5)</span> <span class="n">WikiSkill</span><span class="c chg">wiki에 실패 패턴을 쌓음</span><span class="c chg">SKILL.md를 한 번에 한 곳씩 고침</span><span class="c">고정</span> </div> <p class="small">출처: <code>docs/study/skill-systems-compare.html</code> 그림 1과 7절 비교표.</p> <h3 data-toc-skip>SkillRL (<a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08234" target="_blank" rel="noopener">arXiv 2602.08234</a>, NeurIPS 2026)</h3> <dl class="opt"> <dt>푼 문제</dt><dd>기존 방법은 경험을 궤적이나 메모 그대로 프롬프트에 넣습니다 (ExpeL, Mem0 등). SkillRL은 궤적을 짧은 스킬로 정리합니다. 그리고 모델이 그 스킬을 잘 쓰도록 강화학습을 합니다 <code>PAPERS.md</code>.</dd> <dt>학습 과정</dt><dd>아래 흐름의 ①~④를 거칩니다. ⑤는 학습 중에만 일어납니다.</dd> </dl> <div class="flow" aria-label="SkillRL 학습 흐름"> <div class="fb"><b>① 궤적 모으기</b>ALFWorld 게임 기록 223개</div><span class="ar" aria-hidden="true">→</span> <div class="fb"><b>② 스킬 만들기</b>o3가 기록을 읽고 스킬 55개를 씁니다 (일반 12, 카테고리 32, 실수 11)</div><span class="ar" aria-hidden="true">→</span> <div class="fb hot"><b>③ SFT</b>스킬이 든 프롬프트를 보고 o3의 추론과 성공 행동을 따라 씁니다</div><span class="ar" aria-hidden="true">→</span> <div class="fb hot"><b>④ RL (GRPO)</b>게임을 직접 하고, 성공하면 보상을 받습니다</div><span class="ar" aria-hidden="true">→</span> <div class="fb"><b>⑤ 스킬 추가</b>성공률 0.4 미만 카테고리에 o3가 스킬을 최대 3개 더합니다 (학습 중에만)</div> </div> <dl class="opt"> <dt>스킬을 넣는 방법</dt><dd>에피소드 시작 때 과제 문장의 낱말로 카테고리를 고릅니다. 그다음 일반 스킬 앞 6개, 그 카테고리의 스킬 전부, 실수 앞 5개를 user 메시지에 넣습니다. step 0 요청에는 스킬을 넣지 않습니다.</dd> <dt>프롬프트 구조</dt><dd>매 스텝 user 메시지 하나를 처음부터 새로 만듭니다. 이전 응답은 넣지 않고, 최근 이력 2개만 넣습니다.</dd> <dt>성능</dt><dd>논문은 ALFWorld 성공률 89.9 %를 보고합니다. 우리가 같은 코드로 재현한 값은 79.2 ± 3.3 %입니다. 차이의 원인은 아직 모릅니다.</dd> <dt>알아 둘 점</dt><dd>카테고리 판정 규칙은 과제 문장 12종 중 2종을 다른 카테고리로 보냅니다. 예: "put a hot mug in cabinet"은 heat가 아니라 pick_and_place로 갑니다.</dd> </dl> <h3 data-toc-skip>EvoSkill (<a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02766" target="_blank" rel="noopener">arXiv 2603.02766</a>)</h3> <dl class="opt"> <dt>푼 문제</dt><dd>모델을 학습하지 않고 에이전트의 실력을 올리려 합니다. 실패한 실행을 보고 재사용할 수 있는 스킬 폴더를 만듭니다.</dd> <dt>방법</dt><dd>세 역할이 돕니다. Executor가 문제를 풉니다. Proposer가 실패를 보고 스킬을 새로 만들거나 고치자고 제안합니다. Skill-Builder가 <code>SKILL.md</code>를 씁니다. 검증 점수가 순위 안에 드는 스킬 묶음만 남깁니다.</dd> <dt>스킬을 넣는 방법</dt><dd>Claude Code의 스킬 기능을 그대로 씁니다. 스킬 이름과 설명은 처음부터 system 메시지에 있습니다. 본문은 모델이 Skill tool을 부를 때 대화 중간에 들어옵니다. 대화는 지우지 않고 계속 이어 붙입니다.</dd> <dt>성능</dt><dd>OfficeQA 60.6 → 67.9, SealQA 26.6 → 38.7입니다. BrowseComp에 그대로 옮겨도 +5.3입니다.</dd> </dl> <h3 data-toc-skip>WikiSkill (<a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27454" target="_blank" rel="noopener">arXiv 2608.27454</a>)</h3> <dl class="opt"> <dt>푼 문제</dt><dd>스킬을 고칠 때 근거가 흩어져 있는 문제를 풉니다. 실행 기록을 먼저 wiki 페이지로 정리하고, 그 wiki를 근거로 스킬을 고칩니다.</dd> <dt>방법</dt><dd>Wiki Maintainer가 실패 패턴 페이지를 씁니다. Skill Proposer가 wiki를 읽고 <code>SKILL.md</code> 수정안 하나를 냅니다. 검증 점수가 지금까지의 최고보다 높을 때만 수정을 남깁니다. 아니면 되돌립니다.</dd> <dt>스킬을 넣는 방법</dt><dd>스킬을 고르지 않습니다. 활성 스킬 전체를 Role sentence 바로 뒤에 넣습니다. ALFWorld 템플릿에서는 task 문장이 스킬보다 앞에 있습니다.</dd> <dt>알아 둘 점</dt><dd>공식 코드가 없습니다. 실행 모델은 wiki를 보지 않습니다. 우리 실험의 WikiSkill 방식은 논문의 템플릿을 보고 다시 만든 것입니다.</dd> </dl> <p class="note"><b>세 시스템을 한 환경에서 비교한 방법</b>WikiSkill과 EvoSkill의 스킬 넣는 방식만 SkillRL의 ALFWorld 환경에 옮겼습니다. 스킬 문서는 SkillRL 스킬 뱅크로 만든 합성 <code>SKILL.md</code>입니다 (2-3절).</p> <h2 id="t3" data-toc-text="1-3 vLLM 기초">1-3 vLLM 기초</h2> <dl class="terms"> <dt>prefill과 decode</dt><dd>prefill은 프롬프트 전체를 한 번에 읽고 KV 캐시를 만드는 단계입니다. decode는 응답 토큰을 하나씩 만드는 단계입니다. 재사용은 prefill 계산만 줄입니다.</dd> <dt>KV 캐시 용량</dt><dd>vLLM은 시작할 때 GPU 메모리 일부를 KV 캐시용으로 미리 잡습니다. 우리 설정에서는 41.9만 토큰입니다.</dd> </dl> <figure class="sfig"><div class="chart"> <div class="mem" aria-label="GPU 메모리 나눔"><div class="w" style="flex:14.25">가중치 14.2 GiB</div><div class="kv" style="flex:22.36">KV 캐시 22.36 GiB</div><div class="o" style="flex:3.4">나머지</div></div></div><figcaption class="caption"><b>Figure 1.</b> vLLM에 준 GPU 메모리 (H100의 50 %). 로그 값: 모델 가중치 14.2 GiB, KV 캐시 22.36 GiB = 418,592토큰 (토큰당 약 57 KB) <code>run.log</code></figcaption></figure> <p class="read"><b>해석</b>H100 메모리 80GB의 절반을 vLLM에 주었습니다. 그중 가중치를 뺀 22.36 GiB가 KV 캐시입니다. 토큰 하나의 KV가 약 57 KB라서 캐시에는 41.9만 토큰이 들어갑니다. 2-3절의 빨간 용량선이 이 값입니다.</p> <dl class="terms"> <dt>16토큰 블록</dt><dd>KV 캐시는 16토큰 단위 블록으로 나뉩니다. 재사용도 블록 단위로 합니다.</dd> <dt>앞에서부터 같아야 재사용</dt><dd>블록의 이름(해시)은 그 블록과 앞의 모든 블록 내용으로 정해집니다. 그래서 중간에 한 블록이 다르면, 그 뒤 블록은 글이 같아도 재사용하지 못합니다.</dd> </dl> <div class="chain" aria-label="블록 해시 사슬 예시"> <b>앞 요청</b><div class="row"><span class="bk">system</span><span class="bk">task</span><span class="bk">스킬 1</span><span class="bk">스킬 2</span><span class="bk">스텝 수 2</span><span class="bk">이력</span></div> <b>다음 요청</b><div class="row"><span class="bk hit">system</span><span class="bk hit">task</span><span class="bk hit">스킬 1</span><span class="bk hit">스킬 2</span><span class="bk diff">스텝 수 3</span><span class="bk miss">이력</span></div> </div> <p class="small">초록: 재사용 · 진한 주황: 글이 달라서 다시 계산 · 점선 주황: 글이 같지만 앞 블록이 달라서 다시 계산.</p> <dl class="terms"> <dt>마지막 블록</dt><dd>프롬프트의 마지막 토큰은 항상 새로 계산합니다. 그래서 재사용은 "프롬프트 길이 − 1"을 16의 배수로 내린 값까지입니다.</dd> <dt>용량이 찰 때</dt><dd>새 블록이 필요하면 가장 오래 쓰지 않은 블록부터 지웁니다 (LRU). 요청이 끝나도 블록은 지워지기 전까지 재사용할 수 있습니다. vLLM은 지운 블록 수를 기록하지 않습니다.</dd> <dt>선점</dt><dd>실행 중인 요청의 블록이 모자라면 가장 늦게 들어온 요청을 멈추고, 나중에 처음부터 다시 계산합니다.</dd> </dl> <p>1-1절의 step 2 요청은 1,421토큰이고 928토큰을 캐시에서 가져왔습니다. 직전 요청과는 "Prior to this step, you have already taken N step(s)"의 숫자 N 앞까지 같습니다. 그 지점을 16의 배수로 내린 값이 928입니다.</p> <h2 id="x0" data-toc-text="2-0 측정 방법">2-0 측정 방법</h2> <ul> <li>SkillRL의 공식 실행 경로(verl)는 스텝마다 캐시를 비웁니다. 그래서 verl 없이 같은 프롬프트를 만드는 실행기(하네스)를 따로 만들었습니다.</li> <li>하네스는 공식 경로와 프롬프트 1,259개가 글자 단위로 같았습니다. 성공률은 80.2 ± 2.4 %로 공식 경로의 79.2 ± 3.3 %와 같은 범위였습니다.</li> <li>재사용률은 vLLM이 요청마다 보고한 "캐시에서 가져온 토큰 수"로 잽니다.</li> <li>조건 하나는 게임 64개 × seed 3개입니다. seed는 모델이 응답을 고를 때 쓰는 난수의 시작값입니다 (1-1절). seed가 3개뿐이라서 8~10 %p보다 작은 성공률 차이는 우연과 구별하지 못합니다.</li> </ul> <h2 id="x1" data-toc-text="2-1 재사용이 끊기는 곳">2-1 재사용이 끊기는 곳</h2> <figure class="sfig"><div class="chart" id="c-e2"><div class="plot"></div></div><figcaption class="caption"><b>Figure 2.</b> step 1 이후 요청의 재사용률 (RL 모델, SkillRL 원래 형식). seed 3개 평균. 캐시에서 가져온 토큰 ÷ 프롬프트 토큰</figcaption></figure> <p class="read"><b>해석</b>가로축은 재사용률입니다 (0~1). 공식 경로처럼 스텝마다 캐시를 비우면 프롬프트의 16 %만 캐시에서 가져옵니다. 캐시를 스텝 사이에 남겨 두면 63 %를 가져옵니다. 같은 프롬프트, 같은 모델이고 캐시를 지우는지만 다릅니다.</p> <ul> <li>캐시를 스텝 사이에 남겨 두면 재사용률이 0.160에서 0.633으로 오릅니다.</li> <li>같은 에피소드의 재사용은 "## Current Progress" 바로 뒤의 스텝 숫자에서 끊깁니다. 그 앞부분이 프롬프트의 0.637~0.643입니다.</li> <li>그래서 이 형식에서 재사용률의 실질 상한은 약 0.64입니다.</li> </ul> <h2 id="x2" data-toc-text="2-2 순서를 바꾸면 얼마나 줄고, 무엇을 잃나">2-2 순서를 바꾸면 얼마나 줄고, 무엇을 잃나</h2> <h3 data-toc-skip>정적 분석: 다른 에피소드와 공유하는 앞부분</h3> <figure class="sfig"><div class="chart" id="c-static"><div class="plot"></div></div><figcaption class="caption"><b>Figure 3.</b> 두 에피소드의 step 2 프롬프트가 앞에서부터 같은 토큰 수. 구간 순서별. 이력과 관찰은 짧은 자리표시자로 고정했고, 프롬프트는 1,061토큰입니다. 프롬프트 문자열을 만들어 토큰을 셌습니다 <code>SKILLRL_INTERNALS.md</code> 6.1절</figcaption></figure> <p class="read"><b>해석</b>막대는 두 에피소드의 프롬프트가 처음부터 몇 토큰까지 같은지를 나타냅니다. 길수록 다른 에피소드가 만든 캐시를 많이 쓸 수 있습니다. 원래 순서는 44토큰에서 끝납니다. 두 번째 줄의 task 문장이 에피소드마다 다르기 때문입니다. 스킬을 task 앞으로 옮기면 같은 카테고리끼리 920토큰, 곧 프롬프트의 87 %가 같습니다. 다른 카테고리끼리는 카테고리 스킬에서 갈라져서 263토큰 또는 541토큰입니다.</p> <h4 data-toc-skip class="sh">두 에피소드의 프롬프트를 앞에서부터 비교</h4> <p class="small">G = ## Retrieved Relevant Experience

</span><span class='hl-skill' title='General Principles · 218토큰'>### General Principles
- **Systematic Exploration**: Search every plausible surface or container exactly once before revisiting; prioritize unopened or unseen locations to cover the whole room methodically.
- **Immediate Acquisition**: As soon as a required object becomes visible and reachable, take it before moving elsewhere to avoid losing track or re-searching.
- **Destination First Policy**: After picking up a goal object, navigate directly to the known target receptacle and place it before resuming further search.
- **Track Counts & Progress**: Maintain an internal counter of how many goal objects are still needed; stop searching or terminate episode only when the counter reaches zero.
- **Use State-Changing Tools Early**: For tasks requiring heated/cooled/clean objects, acquire the object, then immediately use the nearest suitable appliance to change its state before any placement.
- **Establish Spatial Relations**: When a goal specifies a relation (under/inside/on), first locate the reference object, adjust its state if needed (e.g., turn lamp on), then search the specified spatial region for the target object or place it there.</span>

<span class='hl-skill' title='카테고리 스킬 (Clean Skills) · 375토큰'>### Clean Skills
- **Phase-Ordered Plan**: Always execute clean tasks in the fixed sequence: 1) locate & acquire target object, 2) bring it to an available water source/sink to clean, 3) navigate to final location, 4) place object.
  _Apply when: As soon as the goal specifies the object must be clean before placement._
- **Pick Before You Wander**: If the target object is visible or discovered, take it immediately; never leave it behind to explore other places, as possession enables direct cleaning and prevents redundant searches.
  _Apply when: After visually confirming the presence of the target object on any surface or inside an opened container._
- **Sink First for Cleaning**: Upon holding the target object, go straight to the nearest sink, basin, or faucet and issue the clean/use command before any placement attempts.
  _Apply when: Once the target object is in hand and its required state is ‘clean’._
- **Systematic Container Sweep**: When the object isn’t found on open surfaces, iterate through all unopened or unexamined containers in the room before revisiting already-checked spots to avoid search loops.
  _Apply when: After initial obvious surfaces are empty and the target object remains unfound._
- **State Verification Before Drop**: Always inspect or infer the object’s state after cleaning; if still not confirmed clean, re-clean before final placement to satisfy goal conditions.
  _Apply when: Immediately after a cleaning action and before placing the object at its target location._
- **Use Location Priors**: Begin search at the most probable category-specific surfaces (e.g., kitchenware on countertop/stove, food on dining table) to minimize exploration steps and avoid aimless roaming.
  _Apply when: At the very start of the task to choose the first search destination for the target object._</span>

<span class='hl-skill' title='Mistakes to Avoid · 278토큰'>### Mistakes to Avoid
- **Don't**: Agent repeatedly revisits the same already-searched locations or containers instead of exploring new ones.
  **Instead**: Maintain an exploration map that records which rooms/containers have been fully inspected and prioritize unvisited or unopened candidates until all reasonable options are exhausted.
- **Don't**: Agent decides a closed container is empty without opening it, causing missed discoveries of target objects.
  **Instead**: Always open and inspect every plausible closed container at least once before ruling it out, using a checklist of unopened containers in the current room.
- **Don't**: Agent ignores or walks away from target objects that are already visible and reachable.
  **Instead**: Embed a perception buffer that immediately queues pick-up actions for visible goal objects and interrupts any ongoing exploratory loop.
- **Don't**: Agent keeps searching after acquiring enough items because it loses track of how many targets have been collected.
  **Instead**: Maintain explicit numerical goals and increment/decrement them on every successful pickup or placement, triggering transition to the next sub-goal when counts are satisfied.
- **Don't**: Agent fails to deliver a held target object to the known destination, instead continuing to wander.
  **Instead**: Adopt a hierarchical policy that, upon holding a goal object, immediately switches to a high-priority ‘deliver-to-goal’ subtask before resuming further search.</span><span class='hl-fixed' title='Progress header (step count) · 34토큰'>

<span class='hl-skill' title='SKILL.md alfworld-core (General Principles 12개 + Mistakes 11개) · 1297토큰'>---
name: alfworld-core
description: Exploration principles and mistakes for every ALFWorld task.
---

## General Principles
- **Systematic Exploration**: Search every plausible surface or container exactly once before revisiting; prioritize unopened or unseen locations to cover the whole room methodically.
  _When: Anytime the goal object count is not yet met and unexplored locations remain._
- **Immediate Acquisition**: As soon as a required object becomes visible and reachable, take it before moving elsewhere to avoid losing track or re-searching.
  _When: Upon first visual confirmation of a goal-relevant object._
- **Destination First Policy**: After picking up a goal object, navigate directly to the known target receptacle and place it before resuming further search.
  _When: Holding any goal object while its target location has been identified._
- **Track Counts & Progress**: Maintain an internal counter of how many goal objects are still needed; stop searching or terminate episode only when the counter reaches zero.
  _When: Throughout multi-instance tasks (e.g., “put two X…”)._
- **Use State-Changing Tools Early**: For tasks requiring heated/cooled/clean objects, acquire the object, then immediately use the nearest suitable appliance to change its state before any placement.
  _When: After picking up an object that must change temperature or cleanliness._
- **Establish Spatial Relations**: When a goal specifies a relation (under/inside/on), first locate the reference object, adjust its state if needed (e.g., turn lamp on), then search the specified spatial region for the target object or place it there.
  _When: Tasks containing spatial prepositions like under, inside, on, in_front_of._
- **Open Before Judging Empty**: Treat any closed container as unexplored; open it and inspect contents before deciding that the goal object is absent.
  _When: Encountering a closed drawer, cabinet, fridge, microwave, etc._
- **Avoid Redundant Rechecks**: Record which locations and containers have been fully inspected; do not revisit them unless new evidence suggests their contents changed.
  _When: After the first full pass of a location or when considering next search target._
- **Plan with Landmarks**: Continuously update and reference a map of known object and container locations to choose shortest paths and prevent aimless wandering.
  _When: Each time a new furniture piece, container, or goal object is observed._
- **Progressive Goal Decomposition**: Break tasks into ordered sub-goals: (1) locate object, (2) obtain or transform it, (3) locate destination/reference object, (4) satisfy spatial relation/placement, completing each sub-goal before moving to the next.
  _When: At the start of every episode and whenever the environment state invalidates the current sub-goal._
- **Efficient Relation Search**: When the goal pairs two objects (A under/on/inside B), restrict search for A to locations near B and vice-versa, instead of treating them independently.
  _When: On goals that mention both a target object and a reference object._
- **Terminate Only On Success**: Issue the 'done' action exclusively after validating that all goal conditions are met; otherwise continue searching or correcting object states.
  _When: Before ending an episode or when the agent believes the task is complete._

## Mistakes to Avoid
- **Don't**: Agent repeatedly revisits the same already-searched locations or containers instead of exploring new ones.
  **Instead**: Maintain an exploration map that records which rooms/containers have been fully inspected and prioritize unvisited or unopened candidates until all reasonable options are exhausted.
- **Don't**: Agent decides a closed container is empty without opening it, causing missed discoveries of target objects.
  **Instead**: Always open and inspect every plausible closed container at least once before ruling it out, using a checklist of unopened containers in the current room.
- **Don't**: Agent ignores or walks away from target objects that are already visible and reachable.
  **Instead**: Embed a perception buffer that immediately queues pick-up actions for visible goal objects and interrupts any ongoing exploratory loop.
- **Don't**: Agent keeps searching after acquiring enough items because it loses track of how many targets have been collected.
  **Instead**: Maintain explicit numerical goals and increment/decrement them on every successful pickup or placement, triggering transition to the next sub-goal when counts are satisfied.
- **Don't**: Agent fails to deliver a held target object to the known destination, instead continuing to wander.
  **Instead**: Adopt a hierarchical policy that, upon holding a goal object, immediately switches to a high-priority ‘deliver-to-goal’ subtask before resuming further search.
- **Don't**: Agent completes spatial placement while skipping required state changes (e.g., cleaning, heating).
  **Instead**: Integrate state precondition checks into the planner so that placement actions are only considered valid after verifying and, if necessary, executing the requisite state-changing operations.
- **Don't**: Agent repeatedly toggles or examines objects that yield no new information or progress.
  **Instead**: Implement novelty or information gain metrics that discourage repeating identical actions unless the environment state has changed since the last attempt.
- **Don't**: Agent mishandles spatial relations (e.g., ‘under’, ‘inside’, ‘behind’) by inspecting only obvious surfaces and ignoring less visible sub-locations.
  **Instead**: During task parsing, generate explicit search targets for all sub-locations associated with the reference object (drawers, shelves, underside) and iterate through them systematically.
- **Don't**: Agent forgets which object it is holding, leading to unnecessary pickups, drops, or misplacements.
  **Instead**: Maintain a dedicated ‘hand inventory’ structure updated after every pickup/drop, and consult it before issuing navigation or interaction commands.
- **Don't**: Agent executes inefficient action sequences by searching for each required object serially rather than batching placements or leveraging proximity.
  **Instead**: Use planning algorithms that group similar subtasks, allowing the agent to collect all required objects in one pass before performing consolidated delivery or transformation steps.
- **Don't**: Agent prematurely terminates or stalls without having observed any candidate objects that satisfy the goal.
  **Instead**: Only allow ‘done’ actions when explicit goal predicates are met; otherwise, continue targeted exploration of remaining unvisited rooms and containers.</span>

<span class='hl-skill' title='SKILL.md alfworld-tasks (카테고리 6개의 Instructions) · 1258토큰'>---
name: alfworld-tasks
description: Step-by-step instructions per ALFWorld task type.
---

## Pick and Place Instructions
1. **Systematic First-Pass Search**: Maintain a checklist of all visible and closed containers/surfaces; open or inspect each unseen candidate exactly once before revisiting any location.
2. **Grab When Seen**: Whenever a needed object is visible and reachable, immediately take it before moving elsewhere—do not leave targets uncollected.
3. **Transform Before Transport**: If the goal specifies a state change (e.g., heated, cooled, cleaned), perform the transformation at the nearest appropriate appliance before heading to the final destination.
4. **Place Before More Search**: When holding any goal object and the target location is known and reachable, navigate there and place it immediately, then resume searching if more items are needed.
5. **Track Counts for Multiples**: Maintain a tally of how many target objects are required, held, and already placed; stop searching only after the placed count meets the goal.

## Look at Object in Light Instructions
1. **Seek Lamp Surfaces First**: Head straight to furniture that commonly hosts a desklamp (desk, sidetable, nightstand) because the target must end up under that light.
2. **Switch Lamp On**: Issue 'use desklamp' as soon as you reach it so the light condition is satisfied before or immediately after handling the target object.
3. **Acquire Or Fetch Target**: If the target is on the lit surface, 'take' it; if found elsewhere, pick it up and carry it back to the lit lamp area.
4. **Systematic Surface Search**: On each candidate lamp surface, look, open nearby containers/drawers once, then move on—ensuring all plausible lamp locations are covered.
5. **Prevent Action Loops**: Avoid toggling the same lamp or re-examining the same empty spot; if no progress after one full check, relocate to a new plausible lamp location.

## Clean Instructions
1. **Phase-Ordered Plan**: Always execute clean tasks in the fixed sequence: 1) locate & acquire target object, 2) bring it to an available water source/sink to clean, 3) navigate to final location, 4) place object.
2. **Pick Before You Wander**: If the target object is visible or discovered, take it immediately; never leave it behind to explore other places, as possession enables direct cleaning and prevents redundant searches.
3. **Sink First for Cleaning**: Upon holding the target object, go straight to the nearest sink, basin, or faucet and issue the clean/use command before any placement attempts.
4. **Systematic Container Sweep**: When the object isn’t found on open surfaces, iterate through all unopened or unexamined containers in the room before revisiting already-checked spots to avoid search loops.
5. **State Verification Before Drop**: Always inspect or infer the object’s state after cleaning; if still not confirmed clean, re-clean before final placement to satisfy goal conditions.
6. **Use Location Priors**: Begin search at the most probable category-specific surfaces (e.g., kitchenware on countertop/stove, food on dining table) to minimize exploration steps and avoid aimless roaming.

## Heat Instructions
1. **Secure Exact Target First**: Always identify and pick up the exact object type named in the goal before interacting with the microwave or destination, ignoring look-alikes (e.g., don’t substitute a mug for a cup).
2. **Systematic One-Pass Search**: Search each plausible surface or closed container once by opening it and inspecting contents; mark searched spots mentally to avoid redundant revisits.
3. **Open Then Heat**: Upon reaching the microwave with the target in hand, always open the door, place the object inside, and execute the heat action before leaving.
4. **No Appliance Before Object**: Do not move to or interact with the microwave or final placement location until the target object is picked up, preventing wasted navigation steps.
5. **Direct Post-Heat Placement**: After heating, navigate straight to the specified destination and place the object once, avoiding extra exploration or detours.

## Cool Instructions
1. **Systematic Object Hunt**: Sweep every unvisited surface and open each closed container until the exact required object is found; never loop over already-checked empty spots.
2. **Confirm Object Match**: After picking up an item, verify it matches the requested type; if not, drop it and resume the search.
3. **Prep Cooling Appliance**: Locate the fridge first and open it so it’s ready for use before or immediately after grabbing the target object.
4. **Enforce Cooling Before Placement**: Do not place the target object in its final location until you have successfully executed a cooling action with the fridge.
5. **Direct Post-Cooling Delivery**: Once the object is cooled, navigate straight to the destination and place it without extraneous detours or re-searching.

## Examine Instructions
1. **Pair Objects Early**: When both the target and desklamp are seen on the same surface, immediately pick up (or leave) the target there and use the desklamp without moving elsewhere.
2. **Grab Target First**: If you see the target but not the desklamp yet, take the target immediately so you can carry it to wherever the desklamp is found.
3. **Shortcut To Tool**: Once holding the target, navigate straight to the nearest known desklamp and issue a single USE command—no intervening searches or detours.
4. **Single Toggle Rule**: Use (toggle) the desklamp only after the target is in hand or co-located; avoid repeated or premature toggles that waste steps.
5. **Explore New Surfaces**: If either the target or the desklamp hasn’t been found, systematically check unvisited surfaces/containers instead of re-inspecting places already confirmed empty.
6. **Lock In Observed Items**: After spotting either required object, do not leave without acting—pick it up (if target) or note its location (if desklamp) to prevent costly backtracking loops.</span><span class='hl-fixed' title='Progress header (step count) · 34토큰'>

name: alfworld-core
description: Exploration principles and mistakes for every ALFWorld task.
---

## General Principles
- **Systematic Exploration**: Search every plausible surface or container exactly once before revisiting; prioritize unopened or unseen locations to cover the whole room methodically.
  _When: Anytime the goal object count is not yet met and unexplored locations remain._
- **Immediate Acquisition**: As soon as a required object becomes visible and reachable, take it before moving elsewhere to avoid losing track or re-searching.
  _When: Upon first visual confirmation of a goal-relevant object._
- **Destination First Policy**: After picking up a goal object, navigate directly to the known target receptacle and place it before resuming further search.
  _When: Holding any goal object while its target location has been identified._
- **Track Counts & Progress**: Maintain an internal counter of how many goal objects are still needed; stop searching or terminate episode only when the counter reaches zero.
  _When: Throughout multi-instance tasks (e.g., “put two X…”)._
- **Use State-Changing Tools Early**: For tasks requiring heated/cooled/clean objects, acquire the object, then immediately use the nearest suitable appliance to change its state before any placement.
  _When: After picking up an object that must change temperature or cleanliness._
- **Establish Spatial Relations**: When a goal specifies a relation (under/inside/on), first locate the reference object, adjust its state if needed (e.g., turn lamp on), then search the specified spatial region for the target object or place it there.
  _When: Tasks containing spatial prepositions like under, inside, on, in_front_of._
- **Open Before Judging Empty**: Treat any closed container as unexplored; open it and inspect contents before deciding that the goal object is absent.
  _When: Encountering a closed drawer, cabinet, fridge, microwave, etc._
- **Avoid Redundant Rechecks**: Record which locations and containers have been fully inspected; do not revisit them unless new evidence suggests their contents changed.
  _When: After the first full pass of a location or when considering next search target._
- **Plan with Landmarks**: Continuously update and reference a map of known object and container locations to choose shortest paths and prevent aimless wandering.
  _When: Each time a new furniture piece, container, or goal object is observed._
- **Progressive Goal Decomposition**: Break tasks into ordered sub-goals: (1) locate object, (2) obtain or transform it, (3) locate destination/reference object, (4) satisfy spatial relation/placement, completing each sub-goal before moving to the next.
  _When: At the start of every episode and whenever the environment state invalidates the current sub-goal._
- **Efficient Relation Search**: When the goal pairs two objects (A under/on/inside B), restrict search for A to locations near B and vice-versa, instead of treating them independently.
  _When: On goals that mention both a target object and a reference object._
- **Terminate Only On Success**: Issue the 'done' action exclusively after validating that all goal conditions are met; otherwise continue searching or correcting object states.
  _When: Before ending an episode or when the agent believes the task is complete._

## Mistakes to Avoid
- **Don't**: Agent repeatedly revisits the same already-searched locations or containers instead of exploring new ones.
  **Instead**: Maintain an exploration map that records which rooms/containers have been fully inspected and prioritize unvisited or unopened candidates until all reasonable options are exhausted.
- **Don't**: Agent decides a closed container is empty without opening it, causing missed discoveries of target objects.
  **Instead**: Always open and inspect every plausible closed container at least once before ruling it out, using a checklist of unopened containers in the current room.
- **Don't**: Agent ignores or walks away from target objects that are already visible and reachable.
  **Instead**: Embed a perception buffer that immediately queues pick-up actions for visible goal objects and interrupts any ongoing exploratory loop.
- **Don't**: Agent keeps searching after acquiring enough items because it loses track of how many targets have been collected.
  **Instead**: Maintain explicit numerical goals and increment/decrement them on every successful pickup or placement, triggering transition to the next sub-goal when counts are satisfied.
- **Don't**: Agent fails to deliver a held target object to the known destination, instead continuing to wander.
  **Instead**: Adopt a hierarchical policy that, upon holding a goal object, immediately switches to a high-priority ‘deliver-to-goal’ subtask before resuming further search.
- **Don't**: Agent completes spatial placement while skipping required state changes (e.g., cleaning, heating).
  **Instead**: Integrate state precondition checks into the planner so that placement actions are only considered valid after verifying and, if necessary, executing the requisite state-changing operations.
- **Don't**: Agent repeatedly toggles or examines objects that yield no new information or progress.
  **Instead**: Implement novelty or information gain metrics that discourage repeating identical actions unless the environment state has changed since the last attempt.
- **Don't**: Agent mishandles spatial relations (e.g., ‘under’, ‘inside’, ‘behind’) by inspecting only obvious surfaces and ignoring less visible sub-locations.
  **Instead**: During task parsing, generate explicit search targets for all sub-locations associated with the reference object (drawers, shelves, underside) and iterate through them systematically.
- **Don't**: Agent forgets which object it is holding, leading to unnecessary pickups, drops, or misplacements.
  **Instead**: Maintain a dedicated ‘hand inventory’ structure updated after every pickup/drop, and consult it before issuing navigation or interaction commands.
- **Don't**: Agent executes inefficient action sequences by searching for each required object serially rather than batching placements or leveraging proximity.
  **Instead**: Use planning algorithms that group similar subtasks, allowing the agent to collect all required objects in one pass before performing consolidated delivery or transformation steps.
- **Don't**: Agent prematurely terminates or stalls without having observed any candidate objects that satisfy the goal.
  **Instead**: Only allow ‘done’ actions when explicit goal predicates are met; otherwise, continue targeted exploration of remaining unvisited rooms and containers.</span>

<span class='hl-skill' title='SKILL.md alfworld-tasks (카테고리 6개의 Instructions) · 1258토큰'>---
name: alfworld-tasks
description: Step-by-step instructions per ALFWorld task type.
---

## Pick and Place Instructions
1. **Systematic First-Pass Search**: Maintain a checklist of all visible and closed containers/surfaces; open or inspect each unseen candidate exactly once before revisiting any location.
2. **Grab When Seen**: Whenever a needed object is visible and reachable, immediately take it before moving elsewhere—do not leave targets uncollected.
3. **Transform Before Transport**: If the goal specifies a state change (e.g., heated, cooled, cleaned), perform the transformation at the nearest appropriate appliance before heading to the final destination.
4. **Place Before More Search**: When holding any goal object and the target location is known and reachable, navigate there and place it immediately, then resume searching if more items are needed.
5. **Track Counts for Multiples**: Maintain a tally of how many target objects are required, held, and already placed; stop searching only after the placed count meets the goal.

## Look at Object in Light Instructions
1. **Seek Lamp Surfaces First**: Head straight to furniture that commonly hosts a desklamp (desk, sidetable, nightstand) because the target must end up under that light.
2. **Switch Lamp On**: Issue 'use desklamp' as soon as you reach it so the light condition is satisfied before or immediately after handling the target object.
3. **Acquire Or Fetch Target**: If the target is on the lit surface, 'take' it; if found elsewhere, pick it up and carry it back to the lit lamp area.
4. **Systematic Surface Search**: On each candidate lamp surface, look, open nearby containers/drawers once, then move on—ensuring all plausible lamp locations are covered.
5. **Prevent Action Loops**: Avoid toggling the same lamp or re-examining the same empty spot; if no progress after one full check, relocate to a new plausible lamp location.

## Clean Instructions
1. **Phase-Ordered Plan**: Always execute clean tasks in the fixed sequence: 1) locate & acquire target object, 2) bring it to an available water source/sink to clean, 3) navigate to final location, 4) place object.
2. **Pick Before You Wander**: If the target object is visible or discovered, take it immediately; never leave it behind to explore other places, as possession enables direct cleaning and prevents redundant searches.
3. **Sink First for Cleaning**: Upon holding the target object, go straight to the nearest sink, basin, or faucet and issue the clean/use command before any placement attempts.
4. **Systematic Container Sweep**: When the object isn’t found on open surfaces, iterate through all unopened or unexamined containers in the room before revisiting already-checked spots to avoid search loops.
5. **State Verification Before Drop**: Always inspect or infer the object’s state after cleaning; if still not confirmed clean, re-clean before final placement to satisfy goal conditions.
6. **Use Location Priors**: Begin search at the most probable category-specific surfaces (e.g., kitchenware on countertop/stove, food on dining table) to minimize exploration steps and avoid aimless roaming.

## Heat Instructions
1. **Secure Exact Target First**: Always identify and pick up the exact object type named in the goal before interacting with the microwave or destination, ignoring look-alikes (e.g., don’t substitute a mug for a cup).
2. **Systematic One-Pass Search**: Search each plausible surface or closed container once by opening it and inspecting contents; mark searched spots mentally to avoid redundant revisits.
3. **Open Then Heat**: Upon reaching the microwave with the target in hand, always open the door, place the object inside, and execute the heat action before leaving.
4. **No Appliance Before Object**: Do not move to or interact with the microwave or final placement location until the target object is picked up, preventing wasted navigation steps.
5. **Direct Post-Heat Placement**: After heating, navigate straight to the specified destination and place the object once, avoiding extra exploration or detours.

## Cool Instructions
1. **Systematic Object Hunt**: Sweep every unvisited surface and open each closed container until the exact required object is found; never loop over already-checked empty spots.
2. **Confirm Object Match**: After picking up an item, verify it matches the requested type; if not, drop it and resume the search.
3. **Prep Cooling Appliance**: Locate the fridge first and open it so it’s ready for use before or immediately after grabbing the target object.
4. **Enforce Cooling Before Placement**: Do not place the target object in its final location until you have successfully executed a cooling action with the fridge.
5. **Direct Post-Cooling Delivery**: Once the object is cooled, navigate straight to the destination and place it without extraneous detours or re-searching.

## Examine Instructions
1. **Pair Objects Early**: When both the target and desklamp are seen on the same surface, immediately pick up (or leave) the target there and use the desklamp without moving elsewhere.
2. **Grab Target First**: If you see the target but not the desklamp yet, take the target immediately so you can carry it to wherever the desklamp is found.
3. **Shortcut To Tool**: Once holding the target, navigate straight to the nearest known desklamp and issue a single USE command—no intervening searches or detours.
4. **Single Toggle Rule**: Use (toggle) the desklamp only after the target is in hand or co-located; avoid repeated or premature toggles that waste steps.
5. **Explore New Surfaces**: If either the target or the desklamp hasn’t been found, systematically check unvisited surfaces/containers instead of re-inspecting places already confirmed empty.
6. **Lock In Observed Items**: After spotting either required object, do not leave without acting—pick it up (if target) or note its location (if desklamp) to prevent costly backtracking loops.</span>

---
name: alfworld-clean
description: How to solve ALFWorld Clean tasks.
---

## When to Apply
- As soon as the goal specifies the object must be clean before placement.
- After visually confirming the presence of the target object on any surface or inside an opened container.
- Once the target object is in hand and its required state is ‘clean’.
- After initial obvious surfaces are empty and the target object remains unfound.
- Immediately after a cleaning action and before placing the object at its target location.
- At the very start of the task to choose the first search destination for the target object.

## Clean Instructions
1. **Phase-Ordered Plan**: Always execute clean tasks in the fixed sequence: 1) locate & acquire target object, 2) bring it to an available water source/sink to clean, 3) navigate to final location, 4) place object.
2. **Pick Before You Wander**: If the target object is visible or discovered, take it immediately; never leave it behind to explore other places, as possession enables direct cleaning and prevents redundant searches.
3. **Sink First for Cleaning**: Upon holding the target object, go straight to the nearest sink, basin, or faucet and issue the clean/use command before any placement attempts.
4. **Systematic Container Sweep**: When the object isn’t found on open surfaces, iterate through all unopened or unexamined containers in the room before revisiting already-checked spots to avoid search loops.
5. **State Verification Before Drop**: Always inspect or infer the object’s state after cleaning; if still not confirmed clean, re-clean before final placement to satisfy goal conditions.
6. **Use Location Priors**: Begin search at the most probable category-specific surfaces (e.g., kitchenware on countertop/stove, food on dining table) to minimize exploration steps and avoid aimless roaming.</span><span class='hl-skill' title='tool 결과: 같은 SKILL.md 안의 공통 구간 (General Principles + Mistakes) · 1280토큰'>

## General Principles
- **Systematic Exploration**: Search every plausible surface or container exactly once before revisiting; prioritize unopened or unseen locations to cover the whole room methodically.
  _When: Anytime the goal object count is not yet met and unexplored locations remain._
- **Immediate Acquisition**: As soon as a required object becomes visible and reachable, take it before moving elsewhere to avoid losing track or re-searching.
  _When: Upon first visual confirmation of a goal-relevant object._
- **Destination First Policy**: After picking up a goal object, navigate directly to the known target receptacle and place it before resuming further search.
  _When: Holding any goal object while its target location has been identified._
- **Track Counts & Progress**: Maintain an internal counter of how many goal objects are still needed; stop searching or terminate episode only when the counter reaches zero.
  _When: Throughout multi-instance tasks (e.g., “put two X…”)._
- **Use State-Changing Tools Early**: For tasks requiring heated/cooled/clean objects, acquire the object, then immediately use the nearest suitable appliance to change its state before any placement.
  _When: After picking up an object that must change temperature or cleanliness._
- **Establish Spatial Relations**: When a goal specifies a relation (under/inside/on), first locate the reference object, adjust its state if needed (e.g., turn lamp on), then search the specified spatial region for the target object or place it there.
  _When: Tasks containing spatial prepositions like under, inside, on, in_front_of._
- **Open Before Judging Empty**: Treat any closed container as unexplored; open it and inspect contents before deciding that the goal object is absent.
  _When: Encountering a closed drawer, cabinet, fridge, microwave, etc._
- **Avoid Redundant Rechecks**: Record which locations and containers have been fully inspected; do not revisit them unless new evidence suggests their contents changed.
  _When: After the first full pass of a location or when considering next search target._
- **Plan with Landmarks**: Continuously update and reference a map of known object and container locations to choose shortest paths and prevent aimless wandering.
  _When: Each time a new furniture piece, container, or goal object is observed._
- **Progressive Goal Decomposition**: Break tasks into ordered sub-goals: (1) locate object, (2) obtain or transform it, (3) locate destination/reference object, (4) satisfy spatial relation/placement, completing each sub-goal before moving to the next.
  _When: At the start of every episode and whenever the environment state invalidates the current sub-goal._
- **Efficient Relation Search**: When the goal pairs two objects (A under/on/inside B), restrict search for A to locations near B and vice-versa, instead of treating them independently.
  _When: On goals that mention both a target object and a reference object._
- **Terminate Only On Success**: Issue the 'done' action exclusively after validating that all goal conditions are met; otherwise continue searching or correcting object states.
  _When: Before ending an episode or when the agent believes the task is complete._

## Mistakes to Avoid
- **Don't**: Agent repeatedly revisits the same already-searched locations or containers instead of exploring new ones.
  **Instead**: Maintain an exploration map that records which rooms/containers have been fully inspected and prioritize unvisited or unopened candidates until all reasonable options are exhausted.
- **Don't**: Agent decides a closed container is empty without opening it, causing missed discoveries of target objects.
  **Instead**: Always open and inspect every plausible closed container at least once before ruling it out, using a checklist of unopened containers in the current room.
- **Don't**: Agent ignores or walks away from target objects that are already visible and reachable.
  **Instead**: Embed a perception buffer that immediately queues pick-up actions for visible goal objects and interrupts any ongoing exploratory loop.
- **Don't**: Agent keeps searching after acquiring enough items because it loses track of how many targets have been collected.
  **Instead**: Maintain explicit numerical goals and increment/decrement them on every successful pickup or placement, triggering transition to the next sub-goal when counts are satisfied.
- **Don't**: Agent fails to deliver a held target object to the known destination, instead continuing to wander.
  **Instead**: Adopt a hierarchical policy that, upon holding a goal object, immediately switches to a high-priority ‘deliver-to-goal’ subtask before resuming further search.
- **Don't**: Agent completes spatial placement while skipping required state changes (e.g., cleaning, heating).
  **Instead**: Integrate state precondition checks into the planner so that placement actions are only considered valid after verifying and, if necessary, executing the requisite state-changing operations.
- **Don't**: Agent repeatedly toggles or examines objects that yield no new information or progress.
  **Instead**: Implement novelty or information gain metrics that discourage repeating identical actions unless the environment state has changed since the last attempt.
- **Don't**: Agent mishandles spatial relations (e.g., ‘under’, ‘inside’, ‘behind’) by inspecting only obvious surfaces and ignoring less visible sub-locations.
  **Instead**: During task parsing, generate explicit search targets for all sub-locations associated with the reference object (drawers, shelves, underside) and iterate through them systematically.
- **Don't**: Agent forgets which object it is holding, leading to unnecessary pickups, drops, or misplacements.
  **Instead**: Maintain a dedicated ‘hand inventory’ structure updated after every pickup/drop, and consult it before issuing navigation or interaction commands.
- **Don't**: Agent executes inefficient action sequences by searching for each required object serially rather than batching placements or leveraging proximity.
  **Instead**: Use planning algorithms that group similar subtasks, allowing the agent to collect all required objects in one pass before performing consolidated delivery or transformation steps.
- **Don't**: Agent prematurely terminates or stalls without having observed any candidate objects that satisfy the goal.
  **Instead**: Only allow ‘done’ actions when explicit goal predicates are met; otherwise, continue targeted exploration of remaining unvisited rooms and containers.

## General Principles
- **Systematic Exploration**: Search every plausible surface or container exactly once before revisiting; prioritize unopened or unseen locations to cover the whole room methodically.
  _When: Anytime the goal object count is not yet met and unexplored locations remain._
- **Immediate Acquisition**: As soon as a required object becomes visible and reachable, take it before moving elsewhere to avoid losing track or re-searching.
  _When: Upon first visual confirmation of a goal-relevant object._
- **Destination First Policy**: After picking up a goal object, navigate directly to the known target receptacle and place it before resuming further search.
  _When: Holding any goal object while its target location has been identified._
- **Track Counts & Progress**: Maintain an internal counter of how many goal objects are still needed; stop searching or terminate episode only when the counter reaches zero.
  _When: Throughout multi-instance tasks (e.g., “put two X…”)._
- **Use State-Changing Tools Early**: For tasks requiring heated/cooled/clean objects, acquire the object, then immediately use the nearest suitable appliance to change its state before any placement.
  _When: After picking up an object that must change temperature or cleanliness._
- **Establish Spatial Relations**: When a goal specifies a relation (under/inside/on), first locate the reference object, adjust its state if needed (e.g., turn lamp on), then search the specified spatial region for the target object or place it there.
  _When: Tasks containing spatial prepositions like under, inside, on, in_front_of._
- **Open Before Judging Empty**: Treat any closed container as unexplored; open it and inspect contents before deciding that the goal object is absent.
  _When: Encountering a closed drawer, cabinet, fridge, microwave, etc._
- **Avoid Redundant Rechecks**: Record which locations and containers have been fully inspected; do not revisit them unless new evidence suggests their contents changed.
  _When: After the first full pass of a location or when considering next search target._
- **Plan with Landmarks**: Continuously update and reference a map of known object and container locations to choose shortest paths and prevent aimless wandering.
  _When: Each time a new furniture piece, container, or goal object is observed._
- **Progressive Goal Decomposition**: Break tasks into ordered sub-goals: (1) locate object, (2) obtain or transform it, (3) locate destination/reference object, (4) satisfy spatial relation/placement, completing each sub-goal before moving to the next.
  _When: At the start of every episode and whenever the environment state invalidates the current sub-goal._
- **Efficient Relation Search**: When the goal pairs two objects (A under/on/inside B), restrict search for A to locations near B and vice-versa, instead of treating them independently.
  _When: On goals that mention both a target object and a reference object._
- **Terminate Only On Success**: Issue the 'done' action exclusively after validating that all goal conditions are met; otherwise continue searching or correcting object states.
  _When: Before ending an episode or when the agent believes the task is complete._

## Mistakes to Avoid
- **Don't**: Agent repeatedly revisits the same already-searched locations or containers instead of exploring new ones.
  **Instead**: Maintain an exploration map that records which rooms/containers have been fully inspected and prioritize unvisited or unopened candidates until all reasonable options are exhausted.
- **Don't**: Agent decides a closed container is empty without opening it, causing missed discoveries of target objects.
  **Instead**: Always open and inspect every plausible closed container at least once before ruling it out, using a checklist of unopened containers in the current room.
- **Don't**: Agent ignores or walks away from target objects that are already visible and reachable.
  **Instead**: Embed a perception buffer that immediately queues pick-up actions for visible goal objects and interrupts any ongoing exploratory loop.
- **Don't**: Agent keeps searching after acquiring enough items because it loses track of how many targets have been collected.
  **Instead**: Maintain explicit numerical goals and increment/decrement them on every successful pickup or placement, triggering transition to the next sub-goal when counts are satisfied.
- **Don't**: Agent fails to deliver a held target object to the known destination, instead continuing to wander.
  **Instead**: Adopt a hierarchical policy that, upon holding a goal object, immediately switches to a high-priority ‘deliver-to-goal’ subtask before resuming further search.
- **Don't**: Agent completes spatial placement while skipping required state changes (e.g., cleaning, heating).
  **Instead**: Integrate state precondition checks into the planner so that placement actions are only considered valid after verifying and, if necessary, executing the requisite state-changing operations.
- **Don't**: Agent repeatedly toggles or examines objects that yield no new information or progress.
  **Instead**: Implement novelty or information gain metrics that discourage repeating identical actions unless the environment state has changed since the last attempt.
- **Don't**: Agent mishandles spatial relations (e.g., ‘under’, ‘inside’, ‘behind’) by inspecting only obvious surfaces and ignoring less visible sub-locations.
  **Instead**: During task parsing, generate explicit search targets for all sub-locations associated with the reference object (drawers, shelves, underside) and iterate through them systematically.
- **Don't**: Agent forgets which object it is holding, leading to unnecessary pickups, drops, or misplacements.
  **Instead**: Maintain a dedicated ‘hand inventory’ structure updated after every pickup/drop, and consult it before issuing navigation or interaction commands.
- **Don't**: Agent executes inefficient action sequences by searching for each required object serially rather than batching placements or leveraging proximity.
  **Instead**: Use planning algorithms that group similar subtasks, allowing the agent to collect all required objects in one pass before performing consolidated delivery or transformation steps.
- **Don't**: Agent prematurely terminates or stalls without having observed any candidate objects that satisfy the goal.
  **Instead**: Only allow ‘done’ actions when explicit goal predicates are met; otherwise, continue targeted exploration of remaining unvisited rooms and containers.</span><span class='mk' title='chat template 토큰 · 2토큰'><|im_end|>

6. **Use Location Priors**: Begin search at the most probable category-specific surfaces (e.g., kitchenware on countertop/stove, food on dining table) to minimize exploration steps and avoid aimless roaming.

<b>## When to Apply</b>
- As soon as the goal specifies the object must be clean before placement.
- After visually confirming the presence of the target object on any surface or inside an opened container.
- Once the target object is in hand and its required state is ‘clean’.
- After initial obvious surfaces are empty and the target object remains unfound.
- Immediately after a cleaning action and before placing the object at its target location.

<b>## Clean Instructions</b>
1. **Phase-Ordered Plan**: Always execute clean tasks in the fixed sequence: 1) locate & acquire target object, 2) bring it to an available water source/sink to clean, 3) navigate to final location, 4) place object.
2. **Pick Before You Wander**: If the target object is visible or discovered, take it immediately; never leave it behind to explore other places, as possession enables direct cleaning and prevents redundant searches.
3. **Sink First for Cleaning**: Upon holding the target object, go straight to the nearest sink, basin, or faucet and issue the clean/use command before any placement attempts.
4. **Systematic Container Sweep**: When the object isn’t found on open surfaces, iterate through all unopened or unexamined containers in the room before revisiting already-checked spots to avoid search loops.
5. **State Verification Before Drop**: Always inspect or infer the object’s state after cleaning; if still not confirmed clean, re-clean before final placement to satisfy goal conditions.
6. **Use Location Priors**: Begin search at the most probable category-specific surfaces (e.g., kitchenware on countertop/stove, food on dining table) to minimize exploration steps and avoid aimless roaming.

<b>## General Principles</b>
- **Systematic Exploration**: Search every plausible surface or container exactly once before revisiting; prioritize unopened or unseen locations to cover the whole room methodically.
  _When: Anytime the goal object count is not yet met and unexplored locations remain._
- **Immediate Acquisition**: As soon as a required object becomes visible and reachable, take it before moving elsewhere to avoid losing track or re-searching.
  _When: Upon first visual confirmation of a goal-relevant object._
- **Destination First Policy**: After picking up a goal object, navigate directly to the known target receptacle and place it before resuming further search.
  _When: Holding any goal object while its target location has been identified._
- **Track Counts & Progress**: Maintain an internal counter of how many goal objects are still needed; stop searching or terminate episode only when the counter reaches zero.
  _When: Throughout multi-instance tasks (e.g., “put two X…”)._
- **Use State-Changing Tools Early**: For tasks requiring heated/cooled/clean objects, acquire the object, then immediately use the nearest suitable appliance to change its state before any placement.
  _When: After picking up an object that must change temperature or cleanliness._
- **Establish Spatial Relations**: When a goal specifies a relation (under/inside/on), first locate the reference object, adjust its state if needed (e.g., turn lamp on), then search the specified spatial region for the target object or place it there.
  _When: Tasks containing spatial prepositions like under, inside, on, in_front_of._
- **Open Before Judging Empty**: Treat any closed container as unexplored; open it and inspect contents before deciding that the goal object is absent.
  _When: Encountering a closed drawer, cabinet, fridge, microwave, etc._
- **Avoid Redundant Rechecks**: Record which locations and containers have been fully inspected; do not revisit them unless new evidence suggests their contents changed.
  _When: After the first full pass of a location or when considering next search target._
- **Plan with Landmarks**: Continuously update and reference a map of known object and container locations to choose shortest paths and prevent aimless wandering.
  _When: Each time a new furniture piece, container, or goal object is observed._
- **Progressive Goal Decomposition**: Break tasks into ordered sub-goals: (1) locate object, (2) obtain or transform it, (3) locate destination/reference object, (4) satisfy spatial relation/placement, completing each sub-goal before moving to the next.
  _When: At the start of every episode and whenever the environment state invalidates the current sub-goal._
- **Efficient Relation Search**: When the goal pairs two objects (A under/on/inside B), restrict search for A to locations near B and vice-versa, instead of treating them independently.
  _When: On goals that mention both a target object and a reference object._
- **Terminate Only On Success**: Issue the 'done' action exclusively after validating that all goal conditions are met; otherwise continue searching or correcting object states.
  _When: Before ending an episode or when the agent believes the task is complete._

<b>## Mistakes to Avoid</b>
- **Don't**: Agent repeatedly revisits the same already-searched locations or containers instead of exploring new ones.
  **Instead**: Maintain an exploration map that records which rooms/containers have been fully inspected and prioritize unvisited or unopened candidates until all reasonable options are exhausted.
- **Don't**: Agent decides a closed container is empty without opening it, causing missed discoveries of target objects.
  **Instead**: Always open and inspect every plausible closed container at least once before ruling it out, using a checklist of unopened containers in the current room.
- **Don't**: Agent ignores or walks away from target objects that are already visible and reachable.
  **Instead**: Embed a perception buffer that immediately queues pick-up actions for visible goal objects and interrupts any ongoing exploratory loop.
- **Don't**: Agent keeps searching after acquiring enough items because it loses track of how many targets have been collected.
  **Instead**: Maintain explicit numerical goals and increment/decrement them on every successful pickup or placement, triggering transition to the next sub-goal when counts are satisfied.
- **Don't**: Agent fails to deliver a held target object to the known destination, instead continuing to wander.
  **Instead**: Adopt a hierarchical policy that, upon holding a goal object, immediately switches to a high-priority ‘deliver-to-goal’ subtask before resuming further search.
- **Don't**: Agent completes spatial placement while skipping required state changes (e.g., cleaning, heating).
  **Instead**: Integrate state precondition checks into the planner so that placement actions are only considered valid after verifying and, if necessary, executing the requisite state-changing operations.
- **Don't**: Agent repeatedly toggles or examines objects that yield no new information or progress.
  **Instead**: Implement novelty or information gain metrics that discourage repeating identical actions unless the environment state has changed since the last attempt.
- **Don't**: Agent mishandles spatial relations (e.g., ‘under’, ‘inside’, ‘behind’) by inspecting only obvious surfaces and ignoring less visible sub-locations.
  **Instead**: During task parsing, generate explicit search targets for all sub-locations associated with the reference object (drawers, shelves, underside) and iterate through them systematically.
- **Don't**: Agent forgets which object it is holding, leading to unnecessary pickups, drops, or misplacements.
  **Instead**: Maintain a dedicated ‘hand inventory’ structure updated after every pickup/drop, and consult it before issuing navigation or interaction commands.
- **Don't**: Agent executes inefficient action sequences by searching for each required object serially rather than batching placements or leveraging proximity.
  **Instead**: Use planning algorithms that group similar subtasks, allowing the agent to collect all required objects in one pass before performing consolidated delivery or transformation steps.
- **Don't**: Agent prematurely terminates or stalls without having observed any candidate objects that satisfy the goal.
  **Instead**: Only allow ‘done’ actions when explicit goal predicates are met; otherwise, continue targeted exploration of remaining unvisited rooms and containers.</pre> <ul> <li>원래 형식은 일반 스킬 앞 6개와 실수 앞 5개만 넣습니다. 합성 문서에는 12개와 11개가 모두 들어간다.</li> <li>WikiSkill 방식은 카테고리 6개를 모두 넣습니다. SkillRL 원래와 WikiSkill·뒤는 step 2에서 가장 크고 그 뒤로 줄어듭니다. 끝난 게임은 더 요청하지 않기 때문입니다. EvoSkill 두 방식은 대화가 쌓여서 스텝마다 커집니다. 용량선을 처음 넘는 스텝은 EvoSkill / EvoSkill·공통 위 순서로 RL 모델 22 / 27, 원본 모델 16 / 16, SFT 모델 17 / 16입니다. 위의 모델 버튼으로 바꿔 볼 수 있습니다.</p> <figure class="sfig"><div class="chart" id="c-hit"><div class="plot"></div></div><figcaption class="caption"><b>Figure 11.</b> 스텝별 실측 재사용률. seed 3개를 합해 계산</figcaption></figure> <p class="read"><b>해석</b>세로축은 그 스텝 요청들의 재사용률입니다. SkillRL 원래(약 0.66)와 WikiSkill·뒤(약 0.85)는 스텝이 지나도 거의 평평합니다. EvoSkill 두 방식은 초반에 0.93~0.97로 가장 높습니다. 그런데 위 그래프에서 토큰 합이 용량선을 넘은 뒤에 크게 떨어집니다. 예를 들어 RL 모델의 EvoSkill은 step 20에서 0.97, step 30에서 0.23입니다. 두 일이 같은 시기에 일어난다는 것만 보입니다. 원인은 아직 확인하지 않았습니다.</p> <ul> <li>EvoSkill 방식은 이전 메시지를 지우지 않습니다. 그래서 스텝이 갈수록 토큰 합이 커지고, step 47~49에서 가장 큽니다.</li> <li>조건별 최댓값은 71.5만~124.4만 토큰입니다. 캐시 용량 41.9만 토큰보다 큽니다.</li> <li>RL 모델 EvoSkill의 스텝별 재사용률은 step 20에서 0.97이고 step 30에서 0.23입니다.</li> <li>원본 모델과 SFT 모델의 EvoSkill run에서는 선점이 run당 116~206번 있었습니다. RL 모델의 EvoSkill run은 0~3번이었습니다.</li> </ul> <h3 data-toc-skip>다시 계산한 토큰</h3> <figure class="sfig"><div class="chart" id="c-recomp"><div class="plot"></div></div><figcaption class="caption"><b>Figure 12.</b> 다시 계산한 토큰 / run (seed 3개 평균). 단위 백만 토큰 (M). 성공률이 낮은 모델은 에피소드가 길어서 요청이 많습니다</figcaption></figure> <p class="read"><b>해석</b>막대가 길수록 run 하나에서 GPU가 새로 계산한 프롬프트 토큰이 많습니다. EvoSkill 두 방식은 7.9M~26.1M 토큰으로, 다른 방식(0.6M~1.5M)의 5배 이상입니다.</p> <h2 id="x4" data-toc-text="2-4 앞부분이 아닌 곳의 재사용">2-4 앞부분이 아닌 곳의 재사용</h2> <p>앞부분 재사용은 프롬프트 앞쪽이 같을 때만 됩니다. 스킬 구간이 프롬프트 가운데에 있으면 쓸 수 없습니다. 그래서 다른 곳에서 계산한 스킬 KV를 가져다 붙이면 무엇이 달라지는지 쟀습니다. 이런 재사용은 CacheBlend 같은 기법이 씁니다.</p> <ol class="steps"> <li>원래 형식 프롬프트에서 구간 다섯 개를 고릅니다. 이 구간을 청크라고 부릅니다.</li> <li>청크의 KV를 원래 자리에서 새로 계산합니다. 이 값이 기준입니다.</li> <li>같은 청크의 KV를 다른 문맥에서 계산합니다. 위치 정보(RoPE)는 원래 자리에 맞게 돌립니다.</li> <li>두 KV의 차이를 잽니다 (K rel). 그리고 그 KV로 응답을 다시 채점합니다.</li> </ol> <dl class="terms"> <dt>K rel</dt><dd>재사용한 K가 원래 K와 다른 정도를 원래 K의 크기로 나눈 값입니다. 0.15는 오차가 원래 크기의 15 %라는 뜻입니다. 층 28개와 KV 헤드 4개의 평균을 구하고, 표본 33개의 중앙값을 씁니다.</dd> <dt>행동이 크게 바뀐 표본</dt><dd>각 모델이 대상 프롬프트에서 직접 뽑은 응답(temperature 0.4)을 그대로 두고, 행동 부분의 log 확률 합이 0.5보다 많이 바뀐 표본 수입니다. <code><action>…</action></code> 형식을 지키지 않은 응답은 틀린 출력으로 보고 세지 않습니다. 모델이 실제로 다른 행동을 골랐는지는 재지 않았습니다.</dd> </dl> <h3 data-toc-skip>청크 위치와 재사용 문맥</h3> <p>이 실험의 대상 프롬프트는 SkillRL 원래 형식의 요청입니다. 표본은 RL 모델 run의 0.02~0.13으로 짧습니다. 청크만 따로 계산한 경우(alone_*)는 0.15~0.42로 깁니다. 같은 청크·문맥에서 세 모델의 차이는 0.05 이하입니다. ②에서도 스킬 청크는 ①과 거의 같습니다. 이력 첫 항목(H)은 원본·SFT 모델에서 0.40~0.43으로 조금 깁니다. 이 두 모델의 궤적에서는 H 청크가 24~29토큰으로 RL 궤적(40토큰)보다 짧습니다.</p> <div class="tbl"><table><thead><tr><th>모델</th><th>궤적</th><th>형식을 지킨 응답</th><th><code>[action></code> 등 깨진 태그</th><th>행동 태그 없음</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>RL 모델</td><td>① = 모델</td><td>① RL 궤적</td><td>33</td><td>0</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td>SFT 모델</td><td>② 자기 궤적</td><td>33</td><td>0</td><td>0</td></tr> </tbody></table></div> <p class="small">표본 33개에서 각 모델이 뽑은 응답의 행동 형식입니다. 형식을 지키지 않은 응답은 틀린 출력입니다. 원본 모델은 ①에서 30개, ②에서 32개가 틀린 출력이라서 차트의 원본 막대는 ①에서 3개, ②에서 1개 응답만 셉니다.</p> <p class="read"><b>해석 · 크게 바뀐 표본</b>막대는 형식을 지킨 응답 중 행동 확률이 크게 바뀐 표본 수입니다. 0에 가까울수록 보정 없이 재사용해도 행동이 거의 그대로입니다. 스킬 청크(G·C·M)에서 RL 모델은 0~1개, SFT 모델은 0~4개입니다. 원본 모델은 3개 중 0개입니다. 행동 목록(A)을 따로 계산하면 RL 모델 12개, SFT 모델 16개로 많습니다. 원본 모델은 표본이 3개라서 이 차트로 다른 두 모델과 비교하지 못합니다.</p> <p class="read"><b>해석 · ② 자기 궤적</b>SFT 모델의 스킬 청크(G·C·M) 값은 ①의 0~4개에서 ②의 0~2개가 됩니다. 이력 첫 항목(H)은 SFT 모델이 ①보다 많습니다 (alone_sys 4 → 9개, prev_step 1 → 6개). 행동 목록(A) · alone_sys는 SFT 모델이 16개에서 10개로 줄어 RL 모델(12개)과 비슷합니다. A · prev_step은 짝이 되는 표본이 RL 10개, SFT 29개로 다릅니다. 원본 모델은 형식을 지킨 응답이 1개뿐이라 비교하지 못합니다. RL과 SFT 모델의 차이를 칸마다 Fisher 정확 검정으로 보면, p < 0.05인 칸은 H · alone_sys(2 vs 9, p = 0.044) 하나입니다. 13칸을 비교한 보정은 하지 않았습니다.</p> <ul> <li>앞 문맥이 조금만 다른 경우(<code>other_*</code>, A · prev_step)는 K rel이 0.02~0.13입니다.</li> <li>청크를 따로 계산한 경우(<code>alone_*</code>)는 K rel이 0.15~0.42입니다.</li> <li>스킬 청크는 따로 계산해 붙여도 행동이 크게 바뀐 표본이 RL 모델 0~1개, SFT 모델 0~4개입니다 (33개 중).</li> <li>행동 목록(A)을 따로 계산해 붙이면 33개 중 RL 모델 12개, SFT 모델 16개가 크게 바뀝니다.</li> <li>원본 모델은 응답 33개 중 30개가 행동 형식을 지키지 않았습니다. 틀린 출력이라서 행동 변화를 세지 않았습니다.</li> <li>각 모델은 자기가 뽑은 응답으로 채점했습니다. 이전 판은 세 모델 모두 RL 모델의 응답으로 채점해서, 원본 모델의 스킬 청크 값이 1~13개로 나왔습니다.</li> <li>② 자기 궤적에서 SFT 모델의 스킬 청크 값은 0~2개, 행동 목록(A) · alone_sys는 10개입니다. RL 모델은 0~1개, 12개입니다.</li> </ul> <h2 id="x5" data-toc-text="2-5 한계">2-5 한계</h2> <ul> <li>환경은 ALFWorld 하나입니다. WebShop과 OfficeQA는 아직 돌리지 않았습니다.</li> <li>WikiSkill과 EvoSkill 방식의 스킬 문서는 합성 문서입니다. 실제 EvoSkill 스킬은 3K~23K 문자로 더 큽니다.</li> <li>seed가 3개라서 8~10 %p보다 작은 성공률 차이는 가려내지 못합니다.</li> <li>잰 값은 토큰 수뿐입니다. 응답 시간과 처리량은 재지 않았습니다.</li> <li>vLLM 0.11.0 한 버전, 게임 64개를 같은 걸음으로 돌린 조건입니다. 실제 서비스처럼 요청이 제각각 들어오는 조건이 아닙니다.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r" data-toc-text="3 연구 질문에 대한 고민">3 연구 질문에 대한 고민</h2> <div class="mine"><b>지금 제 생각</b> <p>제 연구 질문은 스킬 에이전트에서 KV 캐시를 더 많이 다시 쓰도록 스킬을 배치하는 방법(skill schema)을 설계하는 것입니다. 그런데 공통 부분을 앞으로 빼면 끝나는 문제라면, 연구 주제가 될 수 있는지 의문입니다.</p> <p>그래서 두 가지를 생각합니다. 첫째, vLLM과 SGLang 같은 서빙 엔진의 특징을 근거로 KV 캐시를 더 잘 쓰는 방법을 찾는 것입니다 (RQ1). 둘째, 스킬 에이전트마다 상황과 프롬프트 구조가 다릅니다. ALFWorld에 맞춘 방법이 다른 곳에서는 맞지 않을 수 있습니다. 일반화를 할지, 벤치마크마다 해결책을 정리할지 고민입니다.</p></div> <h2 id="plan" data-toc-text="4 skill agent 3년 계획">4 skill agent 3년 계획</h2> <p>KV 재사용과 별개로, skill을 쓰는 에이전트로 3년 동안 무엇을 할 수 있을지 같이 브레인스토밍하려 합니다. 아래 주제들은 출발점일 뿐입니다. 아직 고른 것은 없습니다.</p> <div class="note"><b>방향</b> <ul> <li>thesis 한 줄이 분명해야 합니다. 너무 막연한 주제는 피합니다.</li> <li>skill을 도구로 써서 무언가를 해내야 합니다. 예: skill agent + 실제 transformer, skill로 model editing.</li> </ul></div> <div class="tbl"><table> <thead><tr><th>축</th><th>주제</th><th>질문</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td rowspan="3">A. 모델을 다루는 skill</td><td>Skill → weight 이관</td><td>검증된 skill을 weight edit이나 LoRA로 굳히고, 환경이 바뀌면 다시 text로 되돌릴 수 있나?</td></tr> <tr><td>모델을 고치는 에이전트</td><td>probing·patching·editing 도구를 skill로 가진 에이전트가 LLM의 결함을 스스로 찾아 고칠 수 있나?</td></tr> <tr><td>학습을 운영하는 에이전트</td><td>데이터 선별이나 하이퍼파라미터 요령을 skill로 쌓아 다른 모델의 학습을 돌릴 수 있나?</td></tr> <tr><td rowspan="3">B. skill 획득</td><td>문서·영상에서 추출</td><td>매뉴얼이나 튜토리얼에서 실행 가능한 skill을 뽑으면 시행착오 없이 새 환경에 적응하나?</td></tr> <tr><td>실패에서 skill 만들기</td><td>성공 궤적과 실패 궤적 중 어디서 뽑은 skill이 더 잘 일반화되나?</td></tr> <tr><td>Meta-skill</td><td>skill을 만드는 법 자체를 skill로 배울 수 있나?</td></tr> <tr><td rowspan="3">C. 라이브러리 수명 주기</td><td>간섭과 스케일링</td><td>skill이 몇 개를 넘으면 서로 방해하나? (function(){

    if (parent) parent.appendChild(e);

  }
  function fmt(v, d){ return v.toLocaleString("ko-KR", {minimumFractionDigits: d, maximumFractionDigits: d}); }
  function kfmt(v){ return v >= 1e6 ? fmt(v / 1e6, 2) + "M" : Math.round(v / 1000) + "K"; }

  // ---- tooltip: data-tip marks (hover and keyboard focus); line charts drive it themselves ----
  var tip = document.getElementById("tip");

    var w = tip.offsetWidth, h = tip.offsetHeight;

    var top = y - h - 12; if (top < 8) top = y + 16;
    tip.style.left = left + "px"; tip.style.top = top + "px";
  }
  function showText(text, x, y){ tip.textContent = text; tip.hidden = false; place(x, y); }
  document.addEventListener("pointermove", function(e){
    if (!e.target.closest) return;
    if (e.target.closest("[data-line]")) return;
    var t = e.target.closest("[data-tip]");
    if (!t) { tip.hidden = true; return; }
    showText(t.getAttribute("data-tip"), e.clientX, e.clientY);

  document.addEventListener("focusin", function(e){
    var t = e.target.closest ? e.target.closest("[data-tip]") : null;
